note: Cases tests/conformance/quarantine.json admits we format differently from the oracle. The manifest shrinks when a gap is fixed and grows when one is accepted; this pin makes both a deliberate, reviewable edit. Move it in the SAME commit that moves the manifest, and say which issue the move belongs to. 171 -> 160 is issue #12: explicit ordered list markers are parsed, so the eleven cases whose ordered lists folded into a paragraph now agree with the oracle. 160 -> 103 is issue #18 (the document header): 55 cases whose only divergence was the blank line the formatter inserted between the title and the author line, plus one #9 case and one untriaged case the same read fixed. 103 -> 97 is issue #24 (attribute entry line continuation): the six cases whose continued value became body text now agree with the oracle. 97 -> 95 is issue #21 (YAML front matter): the two cases whose front matter reflowed into a paragraph now come back byte for byte. The third front-matter case stays, relabelled #23: with no closing fence there is no front matter under any reading, and what diverges is the Markdown thematic break. 95 -> 94 is the comparison lens reading a lone tab as the space it renders as (tests/helpers.ts): the tab-expansion case's only divergence was a lens artifact, and the semantic-fidelity check now agrees with what a reader sees. 94 -> 83 is issue #9 (description lists): a description is an item whose recorded lines are written back, so the eleven cases whose descriptions were reflowed as paragraphs now agree with the oracle. 83 -> 82 is issue #23 (Markdown thematic breaks): the front-matter case with no closing fence reads its opening `---` as the break the oracle reads, so its only divergence is gone. 82 -> 19 is issue #16 (underlined section titles): sixty-three cases whose two-line titles were read as a paragraph over a delimited block, which swallowed the rest of the document, now agree with the oracle - the last three of them because an underlined DOCTITLE keeps its underline, which is what leaves compat mode on (DocumentHeaderNode.underline, src/ast.ts). 19 -> 18 is issue #181: a run of two adjacent `+` at a list item's end printed only the byte the tail walk's pop reports, so `lists_test.rb#consecutive list continuation lines are folded#0` failed the reading property; `ListItemNode.trailingContinuation` now prints the other half of the pair beside it and the case matches the oracle's own reading too. 18 -> 16 lands two independent fixes together: issue #64 (`blocks_test.rb#should not recognize fenced code blocks with more than three delimiters#0`) now agrees with the oracle because a four-tilde run opens the OPEN block `openBlockTilde` reads; issue #183 (`test/fixtures/encoding.adoc`) now agrees because narrowing BLOCK_MACRO to Asciidoctor's registered names stops misreading the fixture's own block-macro-shaped line. 16 -> 11 lands two readings together. Issue #80 (the in-document hardbreaks forms): every run of a block carrying the hardbreaks option keeps its source spelling, so `paragraphs_test.rb#should add a hardbreak at end of each line when hardbreaks option is set#0` and `paragraphs_test.rb#should be able to toggle hardbreaks by setting hardbreaks-option on document#0` now render as the oracle renders them instead of being reflowed into one line. And the whole-block rows of the same record: a block holding the unset `{set:name!}` form, and a block holding any attribute reference while the document sets `attribute-missing: drop-line`, keep every run's spelling, because those readings are about which LINE a byte is on. That is issue #236's join half and #80's drop-line half, and it takes `attributes_test.rb#ignores lines with bad attributes if attribute-missing is drop-line#0`, `attributes_test.rb#should drop line with attribute unassignment by default#0` and `attributes_test.rb#should drop line with reference to missing attribute if attribute-missing attribute is drop-line#0` off the manifest.
